title: Enterprise Sales Discovery: Acme Global Expansion

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Jordan, David, thank you both for joining today's session. Our goal is to review Acme's current meeting transcription workflow and understand your enterprise privacy requirements.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Hayes
transcript.text: Right now, our teams spend roughly 6 hours per week manually writing meeting recaps and chasing action items across Jira and Slack. We need automated summaries that integrate directly into our workflow.

transcript.speaker: David Vance
transcript.text: Security is our primary concern. We cannot have employee audio or transcript data used to train public foundation models. We require Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) architecture and SOC2 compliance.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: That aligns perfectly with our architecture. With our BYOK model, your API keys stay strictly client-side or in your private tenant proxy. Meeting audio is processed ephemerally and never retained for model retraining.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Hayes
transcript.text: That sounds promising. What is the pricing model for a 250-seat rollout across our North America engineering and product divisions?

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: For enterprise tiers of 100+ seats, we offer annual tier packages with dedicated onboarding and SLA guarantees. I will follow up with our tailored proposal by Friday.

transcript.speaker: David Vance
transcript.text: Please also send over your standard vendor security assessment questionnaire (VSAQ) and data processing addendum (DPA) so our legal team can begin review.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Hayes
transcript.text: If security signs off, we want to start a 30-day pilot for 25 pilot users starting mid-November.

analysis.executiveSummary: Discovery call with Acme Global Operations and Security leads. Acme expressed urgent need to reduce the 6-hour weekly meeting documentation overhead while strictly enforcing enterprise data privacy via BYOK. Key requirements include SOC2 compliance, ephemeral audio processing, and a 25-user pilot leading to a 250-seat rollout.
keyTakeaways: Customer currently loses ~6 hours per employee weekly on manual recaps and follow-up tracking.
Strict requirement: Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with zero AI model training on customer meeting data.
Target rollout: 25-user pilot in mid-November, expanding to 250 seats across North America.
Follow-up required: Security packet (VSAQ/DPA) and customized commercial proposal.
